A  JUDGMENT (Judgment of the Court was made by R.SUBRAMANIAN, J.)

The Neyveli Lignite Corporation for whose benefit the lands in question were acquired has come up with this appeal under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
2.
The extent of about 7.80 acres of nanja land belonging to the claimant was acquired for the purpose of mining operations by the Neyveli Lignite Corporation.
Section 4(1) notification was issued on 12.03.2000 and the same was followed by the award dated 07.05.2001.
The Land Acquisition Officer granted a sum of Rs.50,000/- per acre as compensation.
3. Aggrieved the claimant sought for reference under Section 19(1) of the Land Acquisition Act.
Upon being referred, the reference was numbered as LAOP.No.116 of 2002 on the file of the Principal Subordinate Court, Vridhachalam.
Thereafter it was transferred to Sub-Court, Neyveli and numbered as LAOP.No.703 of 2008 and again transferred to Sub-Court, Cuddalore and numbered as LAOP.No.632 of 2013.

The Secretary vs Meeranji Ravuthar (Deceased) on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45902008/
2 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 4.
The claimant sought for a compensation under the capitalization method and made a claim on the basis that income from 1 acre of land would be Rs.57,900/-.
5. The 2nd respondent Neyveli Lignite Corporation filed a written statement contending that the income claimed is exaggerated and it would not be more than Rs.20,000/- per acre.
6. At trial before the Sub-Court, the 1st claimant was examined as PW1 and four other witnesses were examined as PW2 to PW5.
Exs. P1
to P7 were marked.

The Executive Engineer of Neyveli Lignite Corporation was examined as RW1, Assistant Director, Agricultural Department,
Vridhachalam, Regulated Market Staff and the Chief Manager of Agriculture and Horticulture Department of the 2nd respondent Corporation were examined as RW2 to RW4.
Exs.R1 to R17 were marked.

7. The learned Sub-Judge upon consideration of the evidence on record arrived at a conclusion that the claimant would have got 45 bags of paddy each weighing 75 Kgs per acre and applying capitalization method https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis computed the compensation at Rs.33,69,600/- for the entire 7 acres 80 cents of land.

In doing so, the learned Sub-Judge adopted the following calculation:
The total extent acquired from the claimant is 3.16.0 hectares= 7.80 acres Yield of paddy per acre per year after deduction is = 45 bags cost of one bag of paddy fixed is = Rs.700/- Cost of 45 bags per acre = 45 x Rs.700 = Rs.31,500/-
Cost of paddy per acre for 7.80 acres per year = Rs.31,500 x 7.80 acres =
Rs.2,45,700/- Value of paddy saplings for 7.80 acres per year = Rs.3000 x 7.80 =
Rs.23,400/-
Value of hay for 7.80 acres per year = Rs.1,500 x 7.80 = Rs.11,700/-

Net Annual income of the claimant for 7.80 acres = Rs.2,45,700/- + 23,400/- +
11,700/- = Rs.2,80,800/-
8.

Relying upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of Haryana Vs. Gurcharan Singh & Another, the learned Sub-Judge fixed the multiplier at '12' and arrived at a sum of Rs.33,69,600/- as https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis aforesaid.

entities.text: State of Haryana Vs. Gurcharan Singh & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned Sub-Judge also rendered a finding that the Neyveli Lignite Corporation being a post-beneficiary will not be entitled to lead evidence in the reference and refused to look in to the evidence placed by it.

9. We have heard Mr.N.Nithianandam, learned counsel appearing for the appellant, Neyveli Lignite Corporation, Mr.T.Sezhian, learned counsel appearing for the respondents 3 to 12/ claimants and Mr.T.Chandrasekaran, learned Special Government Pleader (CS) appearing for the 2nd respondent.

The Secretary vs Meeranji Ravuthar (Deceased) on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45902008/
3 10.
The 1st respondent claimant died pending appeal and his legal representatives were brought on record as the respondents 2 to 11 in this appeal.

11. Mr.N.Nithianandam, learned counsel appearing for the appellant Corporation would vehemently contend that the learned Sub- Judge was not right in adding a sum of Rs.23,400/- as value of paddy saplings as the income from the land.
He would submit that the paddy saplings is an input and it should have been infact deducted.
Addition of https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis value of the paddy sapling is not justified.
He would also add that the LAOP itself was dismissed for default twice and there was a delay of 2245 days in seeking restoration.
Therefore, according to him, the claimant would not be entitled to interest for the delay period.

He would further point out that in view of Section 20(d) of the Land Acquisition Act the Corporation being a person interested in the compensation is entitled to lead evidence and the conclusion of the learned Sub-Judge that the Corporation is not entitled to lead evidence is incorrect.
12.

In fact there was rageing controversy as to the right of the Corporation/ beneficiary which came to an end by virtue of the Full Bench judgment of this Court reported in Neyveli Lignite Corporation -Vs- Rengaswami Reddiar & others reported in AIR 1990 Madras 160.

entities.text: Neyveli Lignite Corporation -Vs- Rengaswami Reddiar & others reported in AIR 1990 Madras 160
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: After the pronouncement of the Full Bench, amendment was brought in, by which the person for whom the land is acquired was included in the definition of person interested by insertion of 20(d) by way of Land Acquisition (Tamil Nadu) Amendment Act, 1989.
Therefore, the right of the Corporation to lead evidence in a LAOP proceedings and the right of the Corporation to file an appeal against the compensation cannot now be questioned.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 13.

Adverting to the merits of the matter, we find that the calculation adopted by the learned trial Judge is justified except for the fact that he has added the value of the paddy sapling for 7.80 acres per acre at Rs.3,000/- (3000 x 7.80).
As we had already pointed out the paddy sapling would be input in paddy cultivation and the value of it could not be treated as income.
Its addition to the income is flawed.
Other than the above we do not see any reason to interfere with the findings of the learned Judge regarding yield of quantum of paddy and the cost of the paddy.
The learned Judge also taken care to deduct the expenditure while arriving at the quantum of yield.
We therefore do not find any reason to interfere with the award made by the learned Judge.
14. Once we accept the contention of Mr.N.Nithianandam, learned counsel that addition of the value of paddy sapling is incorrect, the income per acre after deductions would be Rs.33,000/- per acre.
If we are to multiply the same by 7.80, the total extent of land, the income would be Rs.2,57,400/- .
If we apply the multiplier '12' the total value of the land acquired would come to Rs.30,88,800/-.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 15
. Apart from the above we do not see any error in the award to enable interference in the appeal.
The appeal is therefore partly allowed.
The claimant would be entitled to total sum of Rs.30,88,800/- towards compensation for the value of the land.

Needless to state that the claimants would be entitled to statutory benefits available under Section 23(1)(a) and interest under Section 34 of the Act at 9% for one year after taking possession and 15% thereafter till the date of realisation.
The Secretary vs Meeranji Ravuthar (Deceased) on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45902008/
4
It is also made clear that the claimants would not be entitled to interest for the delay period of 2245 days.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Consequently, the connected miscellaneous petition is closed.

(R.S.M.,J.) (N.
